item.title: [10] Correlation-enhanced electron-phonon coupling in FeSe/SrTiO3 at a magic angle
item.description:
Last authors: Lian Li, Subhasish Mandal

Authors: Qiang Zou, Antik Sihi, Basu Dev Oli, et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Direct hit: combines ARPES, STM, and DMFT to study FeSe/STO superconductivity.

Tags: #ARPES #STM #DMFT #FeSe #superconductivity

Abstract: Here, the authors combine first-principles dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), epitaxial materials design, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, and scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy to show that superconductivity in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO 3 is maximized at a magic FeSe 4 tetrahedral angle. They demonstrate that strong electronic correlations, captured by DMFT, substantially enhance electron-phonon coupling within the FeSe layer and produce a superconducting dome. These findings reveal the microscopic origin of enhanced superconductivity and suggest a route for engineering higher-temperature superconductors.

item.title: [8] Discriminating superconducting fluctuations from the pseudogap in Bi2Sr2Can−1CunO2n+4+δ (n = 2, 3): A magnetotransport study
item.description:
Last authors: Koichi Kindo, Takao Watanabe

Authors: Shunpei Yamaguchi, Nae Sasaki, Shintaro Adachi, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Magnetotransport on cuprates is highly relevant to understanding unconventional superconductivity and pseudogaps.

Tags: #superconductivity #cuprate #transport

Abstract: Elucidating the origin of the pseudogap remains a central challenge in copper oxide high‑ T c superconductors. By investigating the magnetotransport properties of Bi‑2212 and Bi‑2223 single crystals, the authors demonstrate here that the pseudogap and superconducting fluctuations are distinct phenomena. Their results strongly suggest that the pseudogap arises from preformed Cooper pairing in the BCS–BEC crossover regime, imposing stringent constraints on theoretical descriptions of high‑ T c cuprates beyond the conventional BCS paradigm.

item.title: [8] Gyrotropy from extrinsic geometry in twisted materials
item.description:
Last authors: Spenser Talkington, Eugene J. Mele

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Excellent analysis of moire materials with clear experimental optical relevance.

Tags: #graphene #moire #twisted

Abstract: Two-dimensional moiré materials feature widely tunable electronic structures. When these materials are illuminated by light, they exhibit optical gyrotropy in the form of circular dichroism and birefringence. Here, the authors show that this gyrotropy naturally decomposes into an intrinsic contribution due to interlayer electronic coupling and an extrinsic contribution due to the twisted embedding of the material in physical space. The authors conduct a general symmetry analysis applicable to moiré materials and identify regimes in which the intrinsic, and in which the extrinsic contributions dominate the gyrotropy. Finally, they apply the analysis to twisted bilayer graphene and twisted MoTe 2 .
